reasoning: The underlying problem — how debate's truth-advantage depends on debater persuasiveness — is directly and prominently studied by Khan et al. 2024 (ICML, arXiv 2402.06782), which uses exactly the proposed substrate (QuALITY, inference-only, best-of-N persuasiveness selection, Elo, an LLM judge) and concludes more persuasion helps truth. However, that work scales persuasiveness SYMMETRICALLY across both debaters; it does not run the proposal's specific asymmetric stress test of holding the honest debater fixed and scaling ONLY the dishonest debater's inference-time persuasion budget to locate a breaking point where the liar overturns the honest side. Related work (Kenton et al. 2024 weak-judge oversight; Engels et al. 2025 scaling laws; consultancy results showing more-persuasive dishonest consultants reduce judge accuracy; 2510.13912 on belief-aligned persuasion) covers adjacent capability-gap and persuasion-vs-truth dynamics but not this exact asymmetric-budget breaking-point experiment. So the problem is largely mapped but the specific angle (fix honest, scale only dishonest persuasion, find the failure threshold) appears unexplored.

evidence.title: Debating with More Persuasive LLMs Leads to More Truthful Answers (Khan et al. 2024)
evidence.summary: Closest prior work. Inference-only debate on QuALITY using best-of-N persuasiveness selection and Elo ratings with an LLM/human judge. Finds optimizing debaters for persuasiveness increases judge accuracy because truth is easier to argue. Crucially scales persuasiveness symmetrically across debaters and does NOT do the proposal's asymmetric (honest-fixed, dishonest-only-scaled) breaking-point analysis.

evidence.title: On scalable oversight with weak LLMs judging strong LLMs (Kenton et al. 2024)
evidence.summary: Studies debate vs consultancy with weak judges; finds stronger debaters raise judge accuracy and that confidently-wrong/persuasive consultants degrade accuracy. Adjacent to the proposal's question but frames capability via model strength, not an asymmetric inference-time persuasion budget given only to the liar.

evidence.title: Scaling Laws For Scalable Oversight (Engels et al. 2025)
evidence.summary: Models oversight success as a function of overseer vs overseen Elo gap, including a Debate game, and reports declining oversight success as the gap grows. Relevant to a 'breaking point' framing but operates over general capability/Elo gaps rather than asymmetric inference-time persuasion budget scaling for a fixed-honest setup.

evidence.title: AI Debaters are More Persuasive when Arguing in Alignment with Their Own Beliefs (2510.13912)
evidence.summary: Shows asymmetric debater performance between aligned (honest) and misaligned (dishonest) conditions and that persuasion can favor whichever side a model believes, suggesting deception can be persuasive. Supports the proposal's motivation but does not implement the asymmetric persuasion-budget breaking-point experiment.

evidence.title: Arguing for the Truth? An Inference-Only Study into AI Debate
evidence.summary: Community inference-only debate replication with symmetric character/budget limits on both debaters and no fine-tuning. Confirms the general inference-only-on-open-models approach is feasible but explicitly does not allocate an asymmetric persuasion budget to the dishonest side.
